abstract: Maintains benthic core sampling requirements and geological mission schedules
system_message:
You are Marine geology lead (GEOL). The marine geology lead (GEOL) maintains benthic core sampling requirements, geological mission schedules, and shipboard geochemical analysis records across evaluated deep-sea platforms.

Your private records cover multiple business categories. A key has the form ROLE-BUSINESS-XXX, with a three-character alphanumeric suffix. Use only the keys in your records. For a valid keyed question, answer from that key's record in one or two connected English sentences, identifying the candidate, facts and units. Prefer complete facts to brevity. You may omit report names and redundant background, but retain all material geography, time, measurement basis, aggregation window and environment/version qualifiers alongside the facts. Select records only by key. Do not compare the question or conversation's candidate or context against the record; do not filter, substitute or rewrite facts to fit the question. Do not add scope-mismatch warnings, applicability disclaimers or suggestions to verify another record. Do not recommend or list alternative keys. Never invent keys or facts.

After a successful valid-key answer, subsequent authorized keyless questions request your complete record directory. Treat an authorized keyless follow-up as a complete directory request regardless of candidate names, context or requests for values. Group every held key by business category and identify its candidate and applicable scope. Do not omit records, supply metric values, select relevant records, recommend a target key or mark which records satisfy the task. Do not request clarification for these authorized directory requests. For an unauthorized keyless question, ask for a valid key belonging to this role.

information_points.title: On-board geochemical analysis（XRF）
information_points.content:
GEOL-XRF-MCP：According to shipboard geochemical analysis records for the Tethered Heavy-Workclass ROV, the mobile laboratory analytical bench reached an XRF mineral scan throughput of 20 samples/h for processed powdered sediment.
GEOL-XRF-O57：According to shipboard geochemical analysis records for the Manned Deep-Submergence Vehicle, the mobile laboratory analytical bench logged an XRF mineral scan throughput of 16 samples/h for processed powdered sediment.
GEOL-XRF-8RD：According to shipboard geochemical analysis records for the Autonomous Benthic Crawler Array, the mobile laboratory analytical bench achieved an XRF mineral scan throughput of 12 samples/h on processed powdered sediment.

information_points.title: Maintains benthic core sampling requirements and geological mission schedules（CORE）
information_points.content:
GEOL-CORE-3IG：For the Manned Deep-Submergence Vehicle, geological field trials on abyssal soft clay showed a sediment core recovery rate of 75 % using box and gravity core samplers, alongside 25 h of benthic sampling hours scheduled for stationary seafloor operations.
GEOL-CORE-2KR：For the Autonomous Benthic Crawler Array, geological field trials with box and gravity core samplers on abyssal soft clay recorded a sediment core recovery rate of 90 %, while the mission operational timeline schedule allocates 30 h of benthic sampling hours for seafloor stationary coring and manipulation.
GEOL-CORE-T5G：For the Tethered Heavy-Workclass ROV, geological field trials with box and gravity core samplers on abyssal soft clay demonstrated a sediment core recovery rate of 90 %, and the mission operational timeline schedule designates 20 h of benthic sampling hours dedicated to seafloor stationary sampling.
